label: Soul as functional organization: A weaker, potentially reductionist use of the word soul in which…
definition: A weaker, potentially reductionist use of the word soul in which it designates the coordinated powers or organization of a living system, without adding an irreducible intrinsic formal principle. The toy model locates those features in its observable predicates instead of counting them as its distinct SoulAsForm predicate.
note: Comparative terminology only (#329), not attributed to a particular author. Whether a particular hylomorphist's form is functionally reducible is a separate source and metaphysical question.

formal_gap.meaning: In the reading 'soul as functional organization', the word soul names the coordinated powers or organization of a living system without an added irreducible formal principle. In the toy model that organization is represented by Scenario.Integrated p: the system at phase p shows coordinated activity. Integrated is a predicate on the two phases (early, late) of the toy turnover history in TruthCore.Mereology.Vitalism (#329), supplied by each scenario.
examples: The coordinated subsystems of an organism (circulation, metabolism, repair), described functionally.
exclusions: Soul as irreducible principle of substantial unity (SoulAsForm): DISAMB-MEREO-SOUL.
Substantial unity (SubstantialUnity): integration does not by itself make the system one substance (DISAMB-MEREO-UNITY).
open_obligations: Whether a particular hylomorphist's form is functionally reducible is a separate source and metaphysical question.
The same Lean field also carries structural unity (DEF-MEREO-STRUCTURAL-UNITY); the two readings share the observable predicate and differ only in the word's use, not in the model.
No formalization candidate: in the toy model Integrated is an observable input.
